data.narrative:
QuiX Quantum is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Hans van den Vlekkert and Jelmer Renema that has raised €15M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 known peers: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables. The Peer-Median method is not applicable; six same-sector peers exist but none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), and broadening to all-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise. The Stage-Progression method is applicable and serves as the primary anchoring point. Using the €15M total raised as a value proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage step-ups yields an implied valuation of €30M.

The triangulated valuation range is €26M (low), €30M (median), and €34M (high), derived from a single applicable method. This range reflects moderate uncertainty inherent in frontier-stage quantum hardware. Key uncertainties include the maturity and commercialization pathway of QuiX's technology relative to better-capitalized peers, the pace of the broader sector's technical progress, and customer traction not captured in available data. Validation against later-stage funding rounds or exit comparables, should they emerge, would materially refine this estimate.
